_doc: Editorial sources per city for the Phase 2 pipeline. Pilot scope: Melbourne, tier-1 only. Each source carries a `feed_urls` ARRAY — the runner tries each URL in order and uses the first that returns a valid feed. This handles publishers' habit of moving/renaming RSS endpoints without warning, and surfaces the exact HTTP status of every attempt in the run report so we know which endpoint won. The first live Melbourne run on PR #27 saw Broadsheet + Time Out both fail at the single candidate URL; this config widens the search and lets the runner tell us WHY each candidate failed.

verification.notes: First candidate is the conventional WordPress feed endpoint for the Melbourne food-and-drink category. Subsequent entries fall back to the city-level feed and the platform-wide feed (filterable downstream by article URL pattern). If all four 4xx in CI, the next step is publisher partnership or newsletter parsing — see PIPELINE_BUILD.md Layer 3.
City-level feed has been reported as serving ~4 posts/day. /eat-drink/feed is the preferred narrower endpoint (if it exists); city-level is the documented fallback.

Time Out's RSS coverage is the patchiest of the three — they've been retiring feeds in some markets. If all five candidates 4xx in CI, the report will say so explicitly and the resilience plan (newsletter parsing per Layer 3 of PIPELINE_BUILD.md) becomes the next move.
